notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.8.4 'intrinsic-function-name-1 may be specified as a function-identifier without being preceded by the keyword FUNCTION' -> OK §12.3.8.4 13)): within the scope of the containing environment division the named intrinsic may be written without FUNCTION, 'unless specific rules require the use of the keyword FUNCTION'. Code: DataBinder.BindDeclarations fills RepositoryIntrinsics (per-name list, PB974 widened to a list) / RepositoryAllIntrinsic; ConfigurationStep.Produce (DataBinder.Switches.cs:472-473) unions the container's sets into contained units (the 'scope of the containing environment division'); IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction + ReferenceResolver.IsFunctionBearing route a bare NAME / NAME(args) to the intrinsic, and the reserved RANDOM/SIGN/SUM alternative in BindIntrinsic. The one 'specific rule' requiring FUNCTION found in the spec (grep 'keyword FUNCTION') is §13.18.54.3 SR9 (SUM in a report description entry is the RW SUM clause unless preceded by FUNCTION) - honored, pinned by pb924_sum_function_arms_beside_report (FUNCTION SUM INTRINSIC declared; bare SUM in the RD is the clause, FUNCTION SUM is the function, bare SUM(4 5) after the report section is the intrinsic). Probes (out/probe/repo): sr12a.cob FUNCTION PI E ABS INTRINSIC then DISPLAY PI -> 3.141592653589793; gr13n.cob container REPOSITORY FUNCTION MAX ABS INTRINSIC, contained program COMPUTE R = MAX(3, 9, 4) + ABS(S) with S=-7 -> R=16 at 2023 (correct; at 2002 ABS draws COBOL1502 because ABS is a 2014 intrinsic - correct edition window). Not probed: GR13 interaction with >>COBOL-WORDS synonyms, which is GR14's own clause (see GR-12.3.8.4-14). The goldens' header comments cite '§12.3.8 GR13-GR14' without the subclause - imprecise but the numbered GR is right.
